lesson.title: The Short Ball Is Not Permission
lesson.hook: You attack because the ball landed short, then arrive stretched or get passed.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time a ball lands short, check your balance and the opponent’s position before deciding to attack.

pro.label: Nadal, Monte Carlo 2017 final
pro.moment: Nadal aimed his heavy forehand at Ramos-Vinolas's backhand to create space, and was quick to move up the court for the short ball.
pro.read: The attack begins one ball before the short ball.

drill.name: Earned or not
drill.how: Rally. Any ball that lands inside your service line, you may attack only if you're balanced and it's above net height. Otherwise go high and deep. Your partner calls "earned" or "not" after each one.

steps.name: The low, stretched ball
steps.sit: The ball stays below your knee, and you reach it stretched and late.
opts: Flat and deep down the line
Lift it softly over the middle
steps.payoff: Low and late: this ball can't be attacked. Buy time first.
steps.principle: Height and depth buy back the time the stretch took.
steps.why: From below the knee and off-balance, pace and angle both go wrong too often. A high, deep crosscourt gives you net, court and time to recover.

lines.A: Flat from below the knee — into the net.
lines.B: It lands short — they step in and punish it.
lines.C: Soft and short — they step in and attack.
lines.D: High and deep buys time — you're back in the rally.

steps.take: Low and stretched? Go high and deep, then recover.

steps.name: The waist-high ball
steps.sit: Now the ball sits waist-high. You're set, and they're stranded out wide.
steps.q: What does this ball let you do?
opts: Drive it at them, then come in
steps.payoff: Waist-high, set, and they're stranded: now the attack is earned.
steps.principle: Short is an invitation. Height, balance and their position decide if you accept.
steps.why: Everything lines up: a comfortable height, your feet set, and open court. Aim well inside the lines and come in behind it; you don't need a winner.

lines.A: They scramble; you come in and put it away.
lines.B: Straight to them — they pass you as you come in.
lines.C: Too fine — a fraction off, and it's wide.
lines.D: Too safe — they recover and the point starts again.

steps.take: High, balanced, opponent stranded: attack — with margin.

steps.name: The short slice
steps.sit: Your heavy ball draws a short, low slice. You're balanced; they're still deep.
steps.q: How hard do you go at this one?
opts: High through the middle, stay back
Lift an approach and come in
steps.payoff: Balanced but low: approach and come in, rather than go for the winner.
steps.principle: Low contact means lift and margin. Their deep position still invites you forward.
steps.why: The slice stays low, so a flat drive has little room. Lifting a solid approach and closing in uses your time without asking the low ball to do too much.

lines.A: Flat from a low ball — a fraction off, and it's long.
lines.B: Too safe — they recover and the chance is gone.
lines.C: Lift it, come in — their floater is yours.
lines.D: It skims the net and lands short — they push you back.

steps.take: Balanced but low: approach with lift — don't go for the winner.
